samples.summary: The new `currentViewMode !== 'edit'` repaint guard in `setTheme` is bypassed by the unconditional `renderPreview()` in the docChanged updateListener
samples.evidence: `setTheme` (editor.ts:443) guards the repaint with `if (currentViewMode !== 'edit') renderPreview();`, and the new test states the reason is that repainting a hidden pane "would download the mermaid engine for a pane nobody is looking at". But the CodeMirror updateListener at editor.ts:326 (`if (u.docChanged) renderPreview();`) runs regardless of view mode, so in 'edit' mode the very first keystroke calls `preview.render()`, which calls `renderMermaidBlocks()`, which lazy-imports mermaid and runs a full layout pass for every fence in a `display:none` pane — on the typing hot path. The guard therefore achieves nothing beyond the single theme-toggle event, and the stated invariant ("no mermaid engine while the preview is hidden") does not hold.

samples.summary: `passChain` is a process-global, never-reset serialization chain: one stalled load or `mermaid.render()` blocks diagram rendering for every preview on the page, with no timeout
samples.evidence: `let passChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();` (mermaid.ts:359) is module-scoped and every pass for every root is `.then()`-chained onto it (line 408-414). `renderPass` awaits `Promise.all([load(), loadPurifier()])` (line 430) and then `await mermaid.render(...)` (line 468) with no timeout and no abort. A dynamic `import('mermaid')` that stalls (slow/flaky network, a chunk that never settles) or a `mermaid.render()` that never resolves leaves `passChain` pending forever, so every subsequent pass — including for a *different* note opened later, since `loaded`/`passChain` survive unmount — never runs and all placeholders stay stuck on their source fallback. There is no recovery path short of a page reload.

samples.summary: Render failures are cached permanently, so a transient engine error pins "Diagram error" on a valid diagram until the source or theme changes
samples.evidence: `remember(key, result)` at mermaid.ts:486 caches the `{error}` outcome under `${theme} ${source}` exactly like a success. Every later pass short-circuits on that cache entry (collectPending line 373-377 and the re-check at line 458), so a failure that is *not* a deterministic property of the source — e.g. mermaid throwing on `maxTextSize`, a font/measure hiccup, or an internal engine state error — is never retried. The user's only recovery is to edit the diagram text or toggle light/dark. The comment argues failures are deterministic "because passes are serialized", but serialization only rules out concurrency artifacts, not environment-dependent throws.

samples.summary: No cancellation of an in-flight mermaid pass on `dispose()` / unmount: the pass keeps laying out diagrams into a detached tree and holds the global chain
samples.evidence: `dispose()` (editor.ts:481-487) tears down scroll/pointer listeners and destroys the CodeMirror view, but nothing bumps the preview's `passSeq` generation or otherwise cancels a running `renderPass`. `NotePreview` has no dispose at all. After unmount, `superseded()` stays false (no newer render for that root) and `root.contains(el)` is still true for the detached preview, so the pass continues calling `mermaid.render()` for every remaining placeholder — appending/removing `d<id>` hosts on `document.body` and painting into DOM nobody will ever see — while occupying the module-global `passChain` ahead of a freshly mounted note's diagrams.
searchedFor: read NotePreview in packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts for a teardown method

samples.summary: The new `renderPreview()` on theme switch resets the preview's scroll position and, via the split-mode scroll sync, drags the editor pane to the top with it
samples.evidence: `setTheme` now ends with `preview.setTheme(mode); if (currentViewMode !== 'edit') renderPreview();` (editor.ts:442-443). `render()` replaces `this.el.innerHTML` (preview.ts:198), which collapses the pane's scrollHeight and clamps `scrollTop` to 0, firing a scroll event. In 'both' mode the preview's scroll listener `onPreviewScroll = linkScroll(preview.el, editorScroller)` (editor.ts:426) then applies ratio 0 to the editor scroller, so a light/dark toggle jumps both panes back to the top and loses the reading position. Toggling the theme previously did not touch the preview at all.

samples.summary: Two identical mermaid fences in one note produce duplicate element IDs in the document (the cached fragment is cloned verbatim)
samples.evidence: The cache is keyed on `${theme} ${source}` (line 372), so two identical fences hit the same `Rendered` entry and `apply()` inserts `result.node.cloneNode(true)` (line 499) into both blocks. The SVG root carries mermaid's `note-mermaid-N` id and its `<defs>` markers/gradients carry ids derived from it, so the document ends up with duplicated `id` attributes; `url(#…)` / `<use xlink:href="#…">` in the second copy resolve document-wide to the first copy's node. Rendering is visually identical here, but the duplicate-id invariant is broken (a11y/`getElementById` consumers).

finding.summary: `passChain` is a process-global, never-reset serialization chain: one stalled load or `mermaid.render()` blocks diagram rendering for every preview on the page, with no timeout
finding.evidence: `let passChain: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();` (mermaid.ts:359) is module-scoped and every pass for every root is `.then()`-chained onto it (line 408-414). `renderPass` awaits `Promise.all([load(), loadPurifier()])` (line 430) and then `await mermaid.render(...)` (line 468) with no timeout and no abort. A dynamic `import('mermaid')` that stalls (slow/flaky network, a chunk that never settles) or a `mermaid.render()` that never resolves leaves `passChain` pending forever, so every subsequent pass — including for a *different* note opened later, since `loaded`/`passChain` survive unmount — never runs and all placeholders stay stuck on their source fallback. There is no recovery path short of a page reload.

verdict.reason: The structural facts are accurate (module-global `passChain` at mermaid.ts:359, chained at 408-414, no timeout around the awaits at 430/468), but the described failure outcome is unreachable in this repository. Every awaited promise settles and every settled failure is caught so the chain resumes: `import('mermaid').catch(() => null)` (141-144), `import('dompurify').catch(() => null)` (158), `try/catch/finally` around `mermaid.render()` (467-485), and a `.catch()` on the chain itself whose comment states the chain must survive (410-413). Wedging `passChain` requires a promise that NEVER settles; neither `import()` nor `mermaid.render()` produces that, and in production the loader is always the memoized `loadMermaid` (preview.ts:154, 208-211 — `mermaidLoader` is injected only by preview.test.ts). The one concrete sub-claim, a stalled engine load, is also mis-attributed: `loaded` is memoized at 141-144, so every pass awaits the same promise with or without `passChain`; removing the chain would not change the outcome. That outcome is the module's documented graceful degradation — placeholders keep showing escaped source (7-10, 136-139, 149-156) — not a crash, data loss, or corrupted state. The serialization is deliberate and correctness-motivated (351-358: mermaid's config and layout engine are process-global singletons, so overlapping passes would cache diagrams under the wrong theme key). Adding a timeout/abort is robustness hardening against a hypothetical never-settling third-party promise, not repair of a logic bug in the Correctness lane.
